meta.title: Security & Privacy — Aethyr
meta.description: No telemetry, a read-only mode, backups before first save, and a compile gate on batches.

article.heading: Security & Privacy
article.lead: What Aethyr can and cannot do to your project, and the architecture that keeps your work safe.

sections.heading: No telemetry
sections.html:
Aethyr collects zero telemetry. There are no analytics calls, no crash reporters and no usage metrics. Your Blueprint contents and project structure never leave your machine.

The one outbound call in the GitHub build is a once-a-day check of the public GitHub release feed for a newer version. Set AETHYR_UPDATE_CHECK=0 to turn it off. The Fab build has no update check, since Fab handles updates. Installing or updating through apply_update or setup downloads the release zip from GitHub.

sections.heading: Read-only mode
sections.html:
Aethyr can run as a read-only tool. Set one environment variable and Aethyr's typed write tools (adding variables, wiring nodes, saving assets) return an error before touching any file:

AETHYR_READ_ONLY=1

Writes are on by default in every build, Fab included. Set this in any session where you only want to look.

Read-only mode stops Aethyr's typed write tools and bridged Epic writes. console_command is refused too, because a console command can change assets. Set AETHYR_RO_ALLOW_CONSOLE=1 to allow it in a read-only session. run_python_script is on by default and still runs in a read-only session, so set AETHYR_ALLOW_PYTHON=0 in the editor's environment if you need a hard stop. AETHYR_ALLOW_UI=0 does the same for the UI tools.

sections.heading: Automatic backup ring
sections.html:
Before the first save of an existing asset in a session, Aethyr copies the file to <Project>/Saved/AethyrBackups/<Package>-<timestamp>.uasset and keeps the newest 5 copies per asset.

To restore, close the editor and copy a backup over the asset file. Set AETHYR_BACKUP=0 to turn backups off. run_python_script doesn't make backups. Bridged Epic writes are backed up only when AETHYR_EPIC_BACKUP is on (on by default in the Fab build, off in the full build).

Backups cover the first save of each asset per session. Keep your project in source control as well.

sections.heading: Compile gate
sections.html:
Batches (apply_ops, atomic by default) compile once before saving. If the compile has errors, the whole batch rolls back and nothing is written. Single-step writes save as they go, because a half-built graph legitimately has errors. Set AETHYR_STRICT_COMPILE=1 to make single writes refuse to save on compile errors too.

Bridged Epic writes and run_python_script skip the compile gate.

sections.heading: Local only
sections.html:
Aethyr never sends your project data anywhere. The server talks to your AI client over a local stdio pipe and to the editor over loopback (127.0.0.1) only. The only internet access is the optional release check and updates described above, and neither carries project data. Your AI client's own provider still sees whatever the client sends it, so check that client's data policy for NDA work.

When the Epic bridge is on, Aethyr also calls Epic's MCP server on 127.0.0.1 (port 8000 by default).

sections.heading: What setup changes
sections.html:
setup writes to Aethyr's own folder (Plugins/Aethyr) and the project's Saved folder, and to Config/DefaultAethyr.ini only if you pass --deny. It never edits your .uproject, other config files, AGENTS.md, .github/ or the project's .claude/.

In your user profile it adds Aethyr skills and agents under ~/.claude, guidance in the global instruction files of Copilot CLI, Codex and Gemini CLI (only for clients you have), and an MCP entry in each client's user-scope config. By default it lets Claude Code and Gemini CLI call Aethyr's tools without asking each time, and Copilot CLI entries list every tool as enabled. Pass --read-only to keep Aethyr read-only. --dry-run shows the plan first.
